title: Feasibility of the Self‐Reporting Questionnaire‐20 (SRQ‐20) as a Niche‐Targeted Psychiatric Screening Tool for Survivors of Intentional Poisoning in a Resource‐Limited Setting: A Single‐Center Cross‐Sectional Study
abstract: Background Ensuring timely and effective psychiatric care is crucial for patients with intentional poisoning. Given resource constraints in countries like Bangladesh, a screening tool for this patient group can effectively identify appropriate cases and ensure timely care. This study is aimed at assessing whether the WHO‐developed Self‐Reporting Questionnaire‐20 (SRQ‐20) scale can serve as a psychiatric screening tool, compared with the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM‐5), as the gold standard, and determining its cutoff score. Result This cross‐sectional study, conducted in one of the largest tertiary medical college hospitals in Bangladesh, included 105 patients who survived following intentional poisoning. Most of the intentional poisoning survivors were in the age group of 20–29 years, female gender, having a secondary level education, being married, and belonging to a rural area. Using the DSM‐5 criteria, this study found that around 91% of them had psychiatric conditions, with depressive illness being the most prevalent. The mean difference in SRQ‐20 scale scores between the groups of having and not having psychiatric disorders was 5.053 (±0.71), and it was statistically significant. The ROC analysis revealed that the optimal SRQ‐20 cutoff score for predicting having any psychiatric disorders among patients with intentional poisoning was ≥ 6, with a sensitivity of 93.7% and a specificity of 100%. Conclusion At a cutoff of ≥ 6, the SRQ‐20 scale, as a screening tool in resource‐limited hospital settings in Bangladesh, showed promising diagnostic accuracy for identifying DSM‐5‐diagnosable psychiatric disorders among intentional poisoning survivors. However, its validity, reliability, prognostic utility, and optimal thresholds should be further evaluated.
